mainTopic: The laws of כיבוד אב ואם: who pays, how far honor goes, correcting a parent, and giving up honor
overview: The גמרא asks whose money pays when a son feeds and clothes his father. רב יהודה says the son pays, רב נתן בר אושעיא says the father pays, and the רבנן rule that the father pays. The גמרא tests this ruling with several sources: a גזירה שוה that honor must cost the son something (the answer is that he loses work time), a ברייתא about feeding a father מעשר עני, and רבי אליעזר's case of a father throwing a purse into the sea. Next comes the story of רב הונא, who tore silk in front of his son רבה to test him, and the questions about whether that was allowed. Then רב יהודה corrects his father רב יחזקאל's wording of a teaching about mixed groups of condemned people, and שמואל scolds him for speaking to his father that way. A ברייתא teaches that a son should correct his father gently, only by quoting a פסוק. אלעזר בן מתיא and איסי בן יהודה argue about whether a מצוה comes before a father's request, and the הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה. Finally, רב חסדא says a father can give up his honor but a רב cannot. רב יוסף disagrees, and רבא begins to challenge his proof; this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who pays for the father's food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose money is used when a son feeds and clothes his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: From whose money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: when a son feeds his father as part of כיבוד אב, whose money pays for it? This sets up the disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier ברייתא said that כיבוד means feeding, giving drink, clothing and helping the father in and out. It never said who pays. The question is whether the son must spend his own money or only do the work using the father's money.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to honor one's father

phrases.english: From whose [money]?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא that said honoring a father means feeding him, giving him drink, clothing him and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the earlier ברייתא defining כיבוד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the cost of feeding and clothing the father comes from the son's money or from the father's money.

steps.title: Two opinions: son's money or father's money
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the son pays. רב נתן בר אושעיא says the father pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: from the son's money. רב נתן בר אושעיא says: from the father's money.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יהודה, כיבוד includes spending your own money on your father. According to רב נתן בר אושעיא, the son only has to give his effort and service, and the father's own money pays for the food.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: from the son's [money].

phrases.aramaic: רַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: מִשֶּׁל אָב.
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Oshaya said: from the father's [money].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with two opposing views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה: the son's money. רב נתן בר אושעיא: the father's money.

steps.title: The ruling: the father pays
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ruled for רב ירמיה (or his son) that the הלכה follows the view that the father pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן ruled for רב ירמיה, and some say for רב ירמיה's son, like the one who says: from the father's money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a practical ruling: the הלכה follows רב נתן בר אושעיא, so the father's money is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the disagreement into practical הלכה. The rest of the section tests this ruling, first with a challenge and then with a possible proof.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה: the son must serve his father, but the father's money pays for the food and clothing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis ruled for Rav Yirmeya,
and some say, for Rav Yirmeya's son,
like the one who says: from the father's [money].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement of step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה follows רב נתן בר אושעיא: the father's money is used.

steps.title: Honor must cost the son money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא links honoring parents to honoring ה' 'with your wealth', so honoring parents must also cost the son money. If the father pays, what does the son lose?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: It says 'Honor your father and your mother,' and it says 'Honor ה' with your wealth.' Just as there it means with a loss of money, so too here it means with a loss of money. And if you say it comes from the father's money, what loss does the son have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the father-pays view with a ברייתא that uses a גזירה שוה between two verses that both say 'כבד'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honoring ה' 'מהונך' clearly costs money. The ברייתא learns that כיבוד אב ואם must also involve חסרון כיס. If the father pays for everything, the son seems to lose nothing, so the ruling looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A loss of money (literally, a lack in the pocket)
Just as there, so too here (comparison formula)

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: נֶאֱמַר: ״כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּךָ״,
phrases.english: They challenged: It says: "Honor your father and your mother,"
and it says: "Honor the Lord with your wealth."
Just as there, it is with a loss of money,
so too here, it is with a loss of money.
And if you say it is from the father's [money],
what difference does it make to him?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what does the son actually lose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (and ruling) that the father's money pays.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גזירה שוה requires that כיבוד cost the son money. If the father pays, the son has no loss at all.

steps.title: The son loses work time
steps.stepSummary: The son's loss is the work and income he gives up while serving his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the loss of work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even if the father pays for the food, the son still loses money because he stops working in order to serve his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חסרון כיס from the ברייתא does not have to mean spending cash. Giving up time you could have spent earning is also a money loss. This keeps the father-pays ruling in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Stopping one's work (and losing the income)

phrases.english: For the loss of work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the required loss of money as lost work time, not money spent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Honoring 'with a loss of money' means paying out of the son's own pocket.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son's loss is the work he gives up to serve his father, so the father can still pay for the food.
steps.whatToRemember: Even when the father pays, the son's honor costs him something: his time and his work.

steps.title: A ברייתא about relatives sharing tithes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: close pairs such as a father and son may redeem מעשר שני for each other and may feed each other מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Two brothers, two partners, a father and his son, a teacher and his student may redeem מעשר שני for each other and may feed each other מעשר עני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to set up a proof. The proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is that a son may give his poor father מעשר עני. The גמרא will ask how that fits with each view about who pays for the father's food.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money

phrases.english: Come and hear: Two brothers,
two partners,
a father and his son, a teacher and his student,
may redeem second tithe for each other,
and may feed each other the poor man's tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the ruling, the גמרא now looks for a proof for it.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the father's money pays.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא allowing a son to feed his father מעשר עני.

steps.title: The son would be paying his debt with the poor's food
steps.stepSummary: If the son had to feed his father from his own money, giving him מעשר עני would mean paying his own debt with food that belongs to the poor. So the ברייתא seems to prove the father-pays view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is from the son's money, then this son ends up paying his debt with what belongs to the poor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the ברייתא: it only makes sense if the son does not owe his father food from his own money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר עני cannot be used to pay off your own obligations. If the son owed his father food (רב יהודה), feeding him מעשר עני would be using the poor's food for his own debt. Since the ברייתא allows it, the son must not owe that, just as רב נתן בר אושעיא said.

phrases.english: And if you say it is from the son's [money],

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא זֶה פּוֹרֵעַ חוֹבוֹ מִשֶּׁל עֲנִיִּים!
phrases.english: it turns out this one pays his debt with what belongs to the poor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב נתן בר אושעיא's view that the father pays (and against רב יהודה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The permission in the ברייתא to feed a father מעשר עני.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about extra help
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: the ברייתא is talking about extra support beyond what the son owes, so it fits even רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא can be read as talking about something extra the son gives, which he was never obligated to give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even according to רב יהודה, the son only owes his father's basic needs. If he gives more than that, the extra is not a debt, so giving it from מעשר עני is fine. The ברייתא therefore proves nothing, though the ruling from step 3 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case)
Something extra, beyond what is required

steps.confusionAlert: Rejecting the proof does not cancel the ruling. The הלכה still follows the view that the father pays. This step only shows that this ברייתא cannot prove it.

phrases.english: No, it is needed for extra.
phrases.notes: Meaning: the ברייתא is about giving the father more than the son is required to give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא, not the ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא covers the son's required support. It may cover only extra support, which is never a debt, even for רב יהודה.

steps.title: Why curse a son who only gives extra?
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא has רבי יהודה cursing a son who feeds his father מעשר עני. If this is only extra support, why does he deserve a curse?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at what is taught about that ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, 'May a curse come upon one who feeds his father מעשר עני.' If we are talking about extra support, what is wrong with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 8. If the son only uses מעשר עני for extra support, why does רבי יהודה curse him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the son gives מעשר עני only on top of what he owes, so he is not paying his own debt with the poor's food. But a curse suggests he did something truly wrong. That does not seem to fit 'extra' giving.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra, something beyond what is required

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי יהודה here is the תנא quoted in the ברייתא. He is not the same person as רב יהודה, the אמורא who holds that the son pays.

phrases.english: If so, is this what is taught about it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא from step 6 about relatives feeding each other מעשר עני.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
May a curse come

phrases.aramaic: לְמִי שֶׁמַּאֲכִיל אֶת אָבִיו מַעְשַׂר עָנִי.
phrases.english: upon one who feeds his father the poor man's tithe.
And if it is about extra support,
what difference does it make?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that the ברייתא is about extra support
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Giving extra out of מעשר עני does not take anything from the poor, so a curse seems out of place.

steps.title: It is still disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: Even when it is only extra, feeding a father from charity food is degrading to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, it is a degrading thing for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the curse is not about stealing from the poor. It is about shaming the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding a father from food set aside for the poor treats him like a poor man. That is disrespectful even if the son owes nothing. So the curse fits the 'extra support' reading, and step 8 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a degrading or disrespectful thing for him

phrases.english: Even so,
it is a degrading matter for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason behind the curse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The curse must mean the son was paying his own debt with the poor's food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curse is about the shame to the father, which applies even to extra support.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the father throws a purse into the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר teaches that honoring parents goes so far that if the father throws a purse into the sea in front of his son, the son does not shame him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: They asked רבי אליעזר, 'How far does honoring father and mother go?' He told them, 'So far that the father takes a purse and throws it into the sea in front of his son, and the son does not shame him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test who pays for honoring parents. This step quotes the source and sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about the son losing money and staying quiet. The גמרא will ask whose money that purse is, and what this means for the view that the father pays.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
They asked Rabbi Eliezer:
How far does honoring father and mother go?
He said to them:
So far that the father takes a purse
and throws it into the sea in front of him,
and the son does not shame him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new test of the main question after the last proof was pushed away.
steps.raayaObject: Brought against the view (and ruling) that the father's money pays, as step 12 shows

steps.title: If it is the father's money, why would the son care?
steps.stepSummary: If the purse is the father's, the son loses nothing, so the lesson about not shaming him seems pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the son honors him with the father's money, what does the son care?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי אליעזר's case to challenge the view that the father pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson only teaches something if the son is upset about losing money. If it is only the father's money, the son has no reason to be upset. So the source seems to show the son's own money is at stake.

phrases.english: And if you say it is from the father's money,
what difference does it make to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the source quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that honoring parents comes from the father's money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A son has no reason to be hurt by the loss of money that is not his, so the teaching would have nothing to say.

steps.title: The son expects to inherit
steps.stepSummary: The case is about a son who stands to inherit, so he sees the money as his own future money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about a son who is in line to inherit from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even the father's money matters to the son, because one day it would come to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purse belongs to the father now, but the son expects to inherit it. Watching it thrown away hurts him, so holding back from shaming his father is a real test. The source fits the father-pays view after all.

keyTerms.meaning: In line to inherit from him

phrases.english: It is about a son who is fit to inherit from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son only cares if the money is already his.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son also cares about money he expects to inherit, so the source fits the father-pays view.

steps.title: רב הונא tears silk to test his son
steps.stepSummary: A story like רבי אליעזר's case: רב הונא tore silk garments in front of his son רבה to see whether he would get angry.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the story of רבה בר רב הונא. רב הונא tore silk in front of his son רבה. He said, 'I will go and see whether he gets angry or not.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story that matches רבי אליעזר's case of a father wasting money in front of his son. The next steps will ask questions about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא wanted to see whether his son would keep his respect even when watching valuable things destroyed. It is a practical example of the high standard of honor from step 11.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: And this is like the story of Rabba bar Rav Huna.
For Rav Huna tore silk garments
in front of his son Rabba.
He said: I will go and see
whether he gets angry or does not get angry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the case in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father may test whether his son keeps honoring him when he sees property destroyed.

steps.title: Isn't the test a stumbling block?
steps.stepSummary: If רבה got angry, he would sin, and רב הונא would be guilty of putting a stumbling block before the blind.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he would get angry, and רב הונא would break 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story: how could רב הונא risk causing his son to sin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Causing another person to sin is forbidden under לפני עור. Testing a son in a way that could make him disrespect his father seems to break that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not put a stumbling block before the blind; also forbids causing someone to sin

phrases.english: But maybe he would get angry,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָעָבַר אַ״לִּפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל״!
phrases.english: and Rav Huna would break 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא רָתַח וְקָעָבַר אַ״לִּפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רב הונא's action in step 14 was allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's test of his son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The test risked making the son sin, which is forbidden under לפני עור.

steps.title: רב הונא gave up his honor
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא had given up his right to honor ahead of time, so even if רבה got angry, there was no sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had given up his honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that no sin was possible, because the father had already given up his honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father may give up the honor owed to him. Once רב הונא did that, anger from his son would not be a sin, so there was no stumbling block.

phrases.english: Because he had given up his honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son's anger would be a sin, so the test was a stumbling block.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father gave up his honor, so the son's anger would not be a sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a father can give up the honor his son owes him.

steps.title: Isn't tearing silk wasteful destruction?
steps.stepSummary: Tearing good silk seems to break the ban on needless destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he broke the rule of בל תשחית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second problem: ruining valuable silk seems forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without the son's sin, destroying useful things for no real need is forbidden under בל תשחית. Tearing silk seems to be exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on needlessly destroying useful things

phrases.english: But he broke the rule of 'Do not destroy'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב הונא's action, now about the silk itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruining a valuable garment is needless destruction.

steps.title: He tore it at the seam
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tore the silk along the seam, so nothing was really ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: He tore it at the seam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the tear did no lasting damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tear at the seam can be sewn back. So the silk was not truly destroyed, and בל תשחית does not apply.

phrases.english: Because he did it at the seam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tear was at the seam and could be fixed, so nothing was destroyed.

steps.title: Then the test proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the tear was harmless, maybe רבה stayed calm only because nothing was lost, not because of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe that is why he did not get angry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the answer of step 18 ruins the test itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבה could see the tear was only at the seam, he had nothing to be angry about. Then his calm says nothing about how much he honored his father.

phrases.english: But maybe that is why he did not get angry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the tear was at the seam
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A harmless tear gives the son no reason for anger, so the test would show nothing.

steps.title: He did it while his son was already angry
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tore the silk when רבה was already angry about something else, so he would not notice it was only the seam.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did it at a time when his son was angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the test was still real, because רבה was too upset at that moment to notice the tear was harmless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An angry person does not look closely. To רבה it looked like real destruction, so staying calm showed true honor. This answers all three questions and ends the story.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of his anger

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's purse case fits the father-pays view because the son expects to inherit. רב הונא's test was allowed: he gave up his honor, tore at the seam, and did it while his son was already angry so the test was still real.

phrases.english: Because he did it at a time when the son was angry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and closes the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail to the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son could see the tear was harmless, so the test proved nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son was already angry and would not notice, so the test was real.

steps.title: רב יחזקאל teaches the law of mixed condemned groups
steps.stepSummary: רב יחזקאל teaches רמי: if those sentenced to burning get mixed among those sentenced to stoning, רבי שמעון says all are judged with stoning, because burning is harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יחזקאל taught his son רמי: 'If people sentenced to burning got mixed in with people sentenced to stoning, רבי שמעון says they are all judged with stoning, because burning is more severe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. A father, רב יחזקאל, teaches his son a law about death penalties when two groups of condemned people get mixed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We no longer know which person deserves which death. So we give everyone the lighter of the two deaths. For רבי שמעון, burning is the harsher death, so everyone gets stoning.

keyTerms.meaning: those sentenced to death by burning
those sentenced to death by stoning

steps.whyThisMatters: This story appears in the discussion of כיבוד אב. Pay attention to how the son speaks to his father in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרָמִי בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yechezkel taught his son Rami:
Those to be burned [that got mixed] among those to be stoned —
Rabbi Shimon says: they are judged with stoning,
since burning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרָמִי בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about כיבוד אב after the רב הונא and רבה story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When those sentenced to burning and stoning are mixed, רבי שמעון rules all get stoning, because burning is harsher and we use the lighter death.

steps.title: רב יהודה questions the wording of his father's version
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that in this version the stoning group is the majority. So רבי שמעון would not need the reason that burning is harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: His son רב יהודה said to him: 'Father, don't teach it that way. Why does it need the reason that burning is harsher? We could just say it's because most of the people are the stoning group!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה challenges the wording his father used. He shows that the reason given seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The burned among the stoned' sounds like a small burning group mixed into a bigger stoning group. If most are stoning cases, the simple rule of following the majority (רוב) already says to stone them. So why would רבי שמעון need to say burning is harsher?

keyTerms.meaning: I could derive it simply from...

steps.confusionAlert: In 'X among Y', the first group (X) is the small group mixed into the second, bigger group (Y). That is the whole point of רב יהודה's question.
steps.whyThisMatters: Watch how the son corrects his father here. In step 26, שמואל tells רב יהודה that he should not have spoken to his father this way, and that is why the story belongs in the discussion of כיבוד אב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, his son, said to him:
Father, do not teach it this way.
Why specifically [the reason] that burning is more severe?
Let me derive it from the fact that the majority are those to be stoned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the teaching cited in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'הנשרפים בנסקלים' as רב יחזקאל taught it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That wording makes stoning the majority, so following רוב would be enough. That makes רבי שמעון's 'burning is harsher' reason unnecessary.

steps.title: רב יהודה proposes flipping the wording
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה suggests teaching it as 'the stoned among the burned', so the stoning group is the minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Rather, I would teach it this way: those to be stoned mixed among those to be burned.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה fixes the problem he raised by changing the text. He switches the order of the two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now most of the group are burning cases. רבי שמעון still says to stone everyone. Here the reason 'burning is harsher' is truly needed, because we choose the lighter death even against the majority.

phrases.english: Rather, I will teach it this way:
Those to be stoned [mixed] among those to be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem from step 22 by changing the wording of the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The text says the burning group is mixed into a stoning majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The text should say the stoning group is mixed into a burning majority. Then רבי שמעון's severity reason is needed.

steps.title: רב יחזקאל objects from the חכמים' half
steps.stepSummary: With the flipped wording, the חכמים' reason now seems unnecessary. Burning is the majority, so why would they need to say stoning is harsher?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'If so, look at the end: the חכמים say they are judged with burning, because stoning is harsher. Why do they need that reason? Just say it's because most are burning cases!'
steps.whatsHappening: The father pushes back. Your new wording just moves the same problem over to the חכמים' half of the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יהודה's version, the burning group is the majority. The חכמים rule burning, which simple רוב would already give. So their reason 'stoning is harsher' looks just as unnecessary as רבי שמעון's did before.

keyTerms.meaning: say (look at) the end part of the teaching

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי אֵימָא סֵיפָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: If so, say the latter clause:
And the Sages say: they are judged with burning,
since stoning is more severe.
Why specifically [the reason] that stoning is more severe?
Let me derive it from the fact that the majority are those to be burned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new wording from step 23 by using the same kind of question as step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the flipped wording, the חכמים' ruling of burning follows the majority anyway. That makes their 'stoning is harsher' reason unnecessary, which is the same problem in the other half.

steps.title: The חכמים were just answering רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the חכמים gave their reason only to argue against רבי שמעון's reason, not because they needed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'There, the חכמים are answering רבי שמעון: you said burning is harsher. No, stoning is harsher.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends his version. The חכמים were only replying to רבי שמעון's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's reason is truly needed, because he rules against the majority. The חכמים could have relied on רוב. But they chose to argue on רבי שמעון's own terms and deny that burning is harsher. So their wording does not show that they needed the reason, and רב יהודה's version stands.
steps.whatToRemember: In 'X among Y', X is the small group. רבי שמעון's 'harsher' reason only matters when he rules against the majority. That is why רב יהודה flips the text, and he explains that the חכמים' reason was only a reply to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, it is the Sages
who are saying to Rabbi Shimon:
What you said, that burning is more severe — no;
stoning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם רַבָּנַן הוּא דְּקָאָמְרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24 and defends the flipped wording from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the speaker said it that way: the חכמים were replying to רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים' reason seemed unnecessary, because the majority already gives burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים said 'stoning is harsher' only to reject רבי שמעון's claim. So the flipped wording works.

steps.title: שמואל scolds רב יהודה for how he spoke to his father
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה not to speak to his father the way he just did.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: 'Big-toothed one, don't speak to your father like that.'
steps.whatsHappening: After רב יהודה openly corrected his father's teaching, שמואל tells him that this was the wrong way to talk to a father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה had a valid point about the wording. שמואל's complaint is about the way he said it to his father, not about whether he was right. This turns the discussion toward כבוד אב.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'big-toothed one'; a nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Big-toothed one,
phrases.notes: A nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה.

phrases.english: do not speak to your father like that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the way רב יהודה corrected his father in steps 22–25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son should not correct his father in a blunt, direct way.

steps.title: A teaching on how to tell a father he did wrong
steps.stepSummary: שמואל supports his rebuke with a ברייתא: do not tell your father 'you broke the Torah'. Instead say 'this is what is written in the Torah'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: if a person's father was breaking a Torah law, he should not say to him, 'Father, you broke a Torah law.' Instead he says, 'Father, this is what is written in the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל brings a ברייתא as proof that a child must correct a parent in an indirect, respectful way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say to stay silent when a father does wrong. It changes how the correction is said, so the child does not accuse the father directly.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what is written in the Torah

phrases.english: As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה אָבִיו עוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: If one's father was transgressing a Torah matter,
he should not say to him
"Father, you transgressed a Torah matter,"
rather, he says to him:
"Father, so it is written in the Torah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind שמואל's rebuke.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that a son must not correct his father bluntly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about how to tell a father he broke a Torah law.

steps.title: Even that wording would hurt the father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that saying 'this is what is written in the Torah' still causes the father pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is what is written in the Torah'? That still causes him pain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording the ברייתא suggested and says it is still too painful for the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This is what is written' still points straight at the father's mistake, so it feels like an accusation. The גמרא wants a gentler wording that does not embarrass him.

phrases.english: "So it is written in the Torah"?
He is causing him pain!

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ כָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה צַעוֹרֵי קָא מְצַעַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording suggested in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That wording still points directly at the father's mistake, which goes against the goal of not hurting him.

steps.title: Just quote the verse
steps.stepSummary: The fixed wording: 'Father, there is a פסוק in the Torah that says this.' The son quotes the פסוק and lets the father see it for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he should say to him: 'Father, there is a verse written in the Torah like this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a softer wording. The son only mentions a פסוק and does not say his father did anything wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this wording the son only teaches a פסוק. The father can connect it to his own action by himself, and that keeps his dignity.
steps.whatToRemember: A child should correct a parent gently and indirectly, by quoting a פסוק, never by saying 'you sinned'.

phrases.english: Rather, he says to him:
"Father, there is a verse written in the Torah like this."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר לוֹ אַבָּא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son may say 'this is what is written', which points at the father's mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son only mentions a פסוק and does not point at the father.

steps.title: אלעזר בן מתיא: the מצוה comes before serving a father
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר בן מתיא says that if his father asks for water while a מצוה needs to be done, he does the מצוה first, because his father is also obligated in that מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר בן מתיא says: If my father says 'Give me water' and there is a מצוה to do, I set aside my father's honor and do the מצוה, because my father and I are both obligated in the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: what to do when a parent's request and a מצוה come at the same time. אלעזר בן מתיא says the מצוה wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason: the father is obligated in that מצוה too. So the father himself would want his son to do it, and doing the מצוה does not really go against the father.

keyTerms.meaning: I set aside my father's honor

phrases.english: Elazar ben Matya says:
If my father says: "Give me water to drink,"
and there is a מצוה to do,
I set aside my father's honor
and perform the מצוה,
as my father and I are both obligated in the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the laws of כבוד אב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a parent's request clashes with a מצוה, the מצוה comes first, since the parent is also obligated in it.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה: let others do the מצוה if they can
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה says that if others can do the מצוה, they should, and the son should go serve his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בן יהודה says: If the מצוה can be done by others, let others do it, and he should go take care of his father's honor.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion limits the first. If someone else can do the מצוה, the son should serve his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בן יהודה agrees that the מצוה matters. But when others can do it, only the son can fulfill his own כבוד אב, so he should do that. The disagreement is about a מצוה that others are able to do.

keyTerms.meaning: In (taking care of) his father's honor

steps.confusionAlert: איסי בן יהודה does not say a parent always comes before a מצוה. He only says so when the מצוה can be done by others.

phrases.english: Isi ben Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֶפְשָׁר לַמִּצְוָה לֵיעָשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים –
phrases.english: If it is possible for the מצוה to be done by others,
let it be done by others,
and he should go and attend to the honor of his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אלעזר בן מתיא in the case where others can do the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If others can do the מצוה, the son should serve his father instead.

steps.title: The הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה rules that the הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: The הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה settles the disagreement and rules like איסי בן יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, if someone else can do the מצוה, the son should serve his parent. If no one else can do it, the מצוה still comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows איסי בן יהודה: if others can do the מצוה, go honor your parent.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana says:
The halakha is in accordance with Isi ben Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה הֲלָכָה כְּאִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If a מצוה can be done by others, the son should attend to his father's honor.

steps.title: A father can give up his honor, a teacher cannot
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that a father who gives up his honor has truly given it up, but a רב who gives up his honor has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שילא said in the name of רב מתנה, in the name of רב חסדא: A father who gives up his honor, his honor is given up. A רב who gives up his honor, his honor is not given up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching asks who can give up (be מוחל) the honor owed to him. A father can, but a רב cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a father says 'you don't need to honor me', the son does nothing wrong by not doing so. A רב's honor stays in place even if he waives it.

keyTerms.meaning: His honor is given up (the waiver works)

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Sheila said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: that Rav Mattana said that Rav Chisda said:
A father who forgoes his honor,
his honor is forgone.
A rabbi who forgoes his honor,
his honor is not forgone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: giving up honor (מחילה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's waiver of honor works. A רב's waiver does not.

steps.title: רב יוסף: even a teacher can give up his honor
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees and says a רב can also give up his honor. His proof is that ה׳ went before the Jewish people by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: Even a רב who gives up his honor, his honor is given up, as it says: 'And ה׳ went before them by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף argues with רב חסדא and brings a פסוק to show that a teacher can give up his honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ is the Teacher of the Jewish people, yet He Himself led them in the desert, which means He set aside His own honor. So a human teacher should also be able to give up his honor.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
Even a rabbi who forgoes his honor,
his honor is forgone,
as it is stated:
"And the Lord went before them by day."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ הָרַב שֶׁמָּחַל עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב חסדא about a רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רב can also give up his honor, learned from ה׳ leading the people.

steps.title: רבא‎: ה׳'s case is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא questions רב יוסף's proof. ה׳ owns the world and the Torah, so of course He can give up His honor. That does not show a human teacher can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How can you compare? There, the Holy One, Blessed be He, the world is His and the Torah is His, so He can give up His honor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב יוסף's proof from the פסוק. His argument continues past this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says ה׳ can waive His honor because everything, including the Torah, belongs to Him. A human רב's honor comes from the Torah, which is not his own, so the proof seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (literally 'is it so now?')
He can give up His honor

phrases.english: Rava said: How can these be compared?!
There, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
the world is His,
and the Torah is His,
so He can forgo His honor,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's proof from the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the פסוק, not necessarily רב יוסף's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ה׳ owns the world and the Torah, so His ability to waive honor does not carry over to a human teacher.
